$comment: Web UI performance budgets (ADR 151; two JS budgets and the re-baseline ritual per ADR 183). Enforced by `pnpm perf:check` against packages/web/dist/client after a build. initialJsGzipBytes is the worst route's eager graph — what a viewer downloads before the page is interactive, and the number lazy-loading moves. totalJsGzipBytes is every chunk including lazy ones — how much code the product carries, which lazy-loading cannot reduce. Raising a number is a deliberate, reviewed act: justify it in the PR and log the measured cost in docs/perf/web-live-baseline.md. Re-baselined 2026-07-29 from main @ 0acb669 to measured + 15% headroom (initial 124.1 KB on /asks-preview, total 201.7 KB over 29 chunks, largest chunk 98.1 KB, CSS 19.1 KB, fonts 554.5 KB); maxChunkGzipBytes kept its 2026-07-19 value because measured + 15% would have LOOSENED it, and a re-baseline may only tighten (ADR 183). totalCssGzipBytes was RAISED 22000 -> 25300 on 2026-08-04 (measured 21,991 + 15%) — a raise, not a re-baseline, because it loosens: the budget was 99.65% consumed (77 bytes free) before the change that tripped it, and trimming was measured to be unavailable (0 of 373 selectors dead, comments already stripped by the minifier, lightningcss byte-identical). Live.css grew +1,019/-245 lines across 13 shipped office commits in the six days since the last re-baseline. Full evidence + the gzip-CLI-vs-zlib measurement trap in docs/perf/web-live-baseline.md. totalJsGzipBytes RAISED 238000 -> 241000 and totalCssGzipBytes 25300 -> 26400 on 2026-08-12: the goals-grid front door (goalGrid model + GoalGrid view/CSS, ADR: goals-are-the-boards-front-door) measured +~0.9 KB JS / +1.1 KB CSS over budgets that were >99% consumed; the retired swimlane regroup was already deleted in the same change, so no further trim was available. initialJsGzipBytes RAISED 146000 -> 152000 on 2026-08-13: retiring /asks-preview re-chunked the build and made /live's modulepreload list honest — before the deletion the HTML preloaded 12 chunks (126.4 KB) while the true static import closure was 17 chunks / 150.1 KB (protocol dist, asks, OfficeOverlay, wallboard, presenceLabel were loaded eagerly at runtime but never counted). The measured 146.3 KB is not new bytes, it is the first accurate reading; evidence in docs/perf/web-live-baseline.md. initialJsGzipBytes RAISED 152000 -> 156000 on 2026-08-21 (ADR 302 site expansion): the landing page's new typographic sections (SiteNav/LightHero/StreamSection/WhatIs/Teasers) ride the entry chunk because the index route is part of it, so /live's eager graph pays +4.1 KB (146.3 -> 150.4 measured). The lazy remedy was measured and REJECTED: an index.lazy.tsx split moved the sections out of entry but rolldown re-chunked shared modules (fileRoute +10.8 KB, jsx-runtime +2.9 KB emerged as separate eager chunks) for a WORSE initial (152.1 KB) and +26 KB total — do not re-chase without new evidence. Raise covers measured 154,010 bytes + ~1.2% slack, matching the 2026-08-12 precedent; evidence in docs/perf/web-live-baseline.md. totalCssGzipBytes SPLIT into appCssGzipBytes + siteCssGzipBytes + sharedCssGzipBytes on 2026-08-24 (ADR 313, Delight 0): the single ceiling had 6 bytes free and its two consumers share a build but not a fate — the office app (Live.css alone is 15,810 gzip) and the eight-route public site were competing for one number set when the site was one page, which is how two raises accumulated with no re-baseline. Each budget is that surface's measured gzip + 15% (app 21,492 -> 24,700; site 2,538 -> 2,900; shared global/brand 2,364 -> 2,700) — a deliberate loosening under ADR 183's ritual, recorded as such, because a re-baseline may only tighten and could not have produced runway. Bundles are classified by pre-hash basename against cssBundles below; an unlisted bundle FAILS the gate (same design as the font allowlist) so a new stylesheet is classified deliberately, never silently. Evidence incl. the canvas-substitutability measurement that rejected the alternative route in docs/perf/web-live-baseline.md. totalJsGzipBytes RAISED 241000 -> 246000 on 2026-08-24 for the lazy Shared Seeds drawer: main measured 240,813 B; the feature measures 243,065 B total and 155,194 B eager, so only the total ceiling moves to measured + ~1.2% headroom. The raise was correct triage — main was red and every rebased PR with it — but its premise, "no lazy remedy exists", held only for #1158's own bytes. Those are 243 B and all feature (applyTierClock, the answerableCount loudness guard, the lapsed note's copy), unshaveable without taking the honesty out of the surface. The remedy was elsewhere: BoardOverlay's header has said since it was written that the board is "kept out of /live's eager graph (ADR 151)", but only the heavy inner Board ever was — the 219-line modal shell, and with it useBoardData/goalGrid/boardOverlayMath, rode the entry chunk on a route that renders none of it until a reader reaches for the wall, behind an already-conditional {boardOpen && ...}. Making the SHELL lazy too (live.tsx LazyBoardOverlay + preloadBoardOverlay, which keeps the old hover/focus preload promise and now warms both halves) measured 155,960 -> 152,540 B eager, -3,439 B, about 14x what #1158 borrowed. Per ADR 183 the total moved the other way as predicted, 249,509 -> 250,547 B (+~1 KB of per-chunk overhead, 36 -> 38 chunks), still inside the 252000 ceiling. New number is measured 152,540 + the CI gzip delta + ~1.2% slack per the 2026-08-12 precedent, leaving ~1.9 KB of true headroom where 279 B had made any web change a coin flip against CI. Two traps found measuring this, both cost time: `perf:check` does NOT build, it only reads packages/web/dist/client, so a measurement taken without `pnpm --filter @musterd/web build` first is the previous tree's dist and can show a nonexistent 0 B delta; and a PR whose own gates read N KB against an N KB ceiling will read OVER on main, which is the raise-above's process finding, kept. Verified: 816/816 web tests, typecheck, lint (0 errors), prettier, tokens:check, a11y:check 14 routes 0 below AA including the connected /live asks-sheet sweep, and the overlay opened for real against a fixture team. Evidence in docs/perf/web-live-baseline.md. totalJsGzipBytes RAISED 252000 -> 255000 on 2026-09-02 for the musterd.io agent surfaces (markdown mirrors, llms-full.txt, blog RSS; PR #1177): the feature is build-time and measures +28 B of client JS -- markdownAlternate()/feedAlternate() and the route links arrays that announce a page's markdown mirror from its own head -- against a ceiling main was consuming to 99.96% on CI (main @ 0c4315fa read 246.0 KiB against 246.1 KiB green, the branch 246.1 KiB red, +28 B measured identically local and CI). ADR 183 forbids the only cheaper remedies by construction: lazy-loading cannot move total, and there is nothing to delete -- an import.meta.env.SSR guard on the two helpers was measured as available and REJECTED, because it drops the tags from the client build and React removes them from the head at hydration, so a JS-rendering crawler watches the announcement disappear. Re-baseline checked first and unavailable (measured + 15% loosens; a re-baseline may only tighten). CI-measured + ~1.2% per the 2026-08-24/25/31 precedents, leaving ~3.8 KB of true headroom where under 100 B had made any web change a coin flip. Fourth total raise since 2026-08-24 with no re-baseline between them -- the trend is logged as a trend in docs/perf/web-live-baseline.md. initialJsGzipBytes RE-BASELINED 154500 -> 144000 on 2026-09-02, a TIGHTENING (ADR 183 permits only that direction) worth 10.5 KB — the largest single move this budget has seen, and it corrects a wrong conclusion of mine recorded the same day. The 2026-09-02 entry directly above says real headroom "needs architecture (defer roster parsing), not an import tidy", because packages/web/src/live/format.ts value-imports three pure helpers from the @musterd/protocol BARREL while live/client.ts also imports the zod schemas it parses the roster with — so tidying format.ts alone looked pointless. Measured, that was backwards: format.ts was the ONLY eager path into zod. Deep-importing its three helpers from the module that owns them (normalizeModelId/reviewGrade from @musterd/protocol/model, resolvePosture from @musterd/protocol/posture, two new subpath exports) let rolldown tree-shake zod out of the shared protocol chunk entirely: the eager dist- chunk falls 23,031 -> 10,048 B gzip, zod moves to a lazy chunk fetched with the roster rather than before first paint, and /live's eager graph goes 154,197 -> 141,341 B (150.6 -> 138.0 KiB), 13 chunks either side. Nothing was deleted and no parse was made lazier — client.ts still validates every roster row exactly as before, and the 964 web tests are unchanged and green. The architectural remedy the old note described is NOT needed for these bytes and should not be chased for them. Per ADR 183 the total moved the other way as predicted, 247.1 -> 247.8 KiB (+~0.7 KiB of per-chunk overhead, 37 -> 38 chunks), still inside the 255000 ceiling — but that ceiling is now 99.5% consumed and is the one to watch. New number is measured 141,341 + the known ~0.7 KB CI gzip delta + ~1.2% slack, per the 2026-08-12 precedent. Deliberately NOT padded further for the dwell work in flight: a budget sized for work that has not landed is the calibration failure this file keeps re-learning. Evidence in docs/perf/web-live-baseline.md. A THIRD LEVER on totalJsGzipBytes, named 2026-09-03 because the sentence above about "deleting code or dropping a dependency" reads as an exhaustive pair and is not one: per-chunk overhead is real and additive (splitting cost ~1 KB at 36->38 chunks and ~0.7 KB at 37->38, both measured and recorded here), so UN-splitting lowers total and ADR 183 does not forbid it. The obvious instrument was measured and REJECTED: a build.rollupOptions.output.manualChunks grouping the four near-empty public-site route stubs (docs._slug/docs.index/blog._slug/blog.index, 275-327 B gzip each) made BOTH budgets worse -- total 248.3 -> 249.7 KB (RED) and initial 138.6 -> 139.9 KB, chunk count unchanged at 38 -- because the stubs TanStack Start emits are VIRTUAL modules from its route-splitting, so a predicate matching src/routes/*.tsx cannot reach them and instead hoisted 16.1 KB of real page code out of the entry chunk into a new one, paying fresh overhead. Same shape as the 2026-08-21 index.lazy.tsx rejection: this build's chunk graph cannot be steered from outside by naming source files. The lever stands; that instrument does not. The dependency arm is closed too -- react, react-dom, two TanStack, two @fontsource and the workspace protocol, nothing droppable without an architecture change. Also measured that day: the ritual itself cannot repair this budget, since a re-baseline may only tighten, measured + 15% loosens, and tightening toward measured leaves zero headroom against the ~0.7 KB CI gzip delta. Five raises since 2026-08-24 with no tightening between them is the finding. The 2026-09-02 entry above got zod out of the EAGER graph by deep-importing three helpers from @musterd/protocol/model and /posture, but zod stayed in the product: those two subpath modules import their vocabularies from acts.ts, which builds z.enums at module scope, so a lazy 13.5 KB `posture` chunk was still fetched with the roster and the protocol barrel chunk still carried its whole z.object(...) graph. The repayment is structural rather than an import tidy: every closed set and pure derivation the browser reads now lives in a validator-free `*.wire.ts` module that the zod module beside it builds its enum FROM and re-exports (acts/ask/capabilities/envelope/goals/lanes/offline/posture/seeds/working-hours), the eight web parse sites read through `protocol/guards.ts`, and one new subpath `@musterd/protocol/wire` is the browser's whole door into the contract. Measured on the branch: zod is absent from every chunk in dist/client (grep for ZodError finds nothing), total 249.1 -> 228.6 KiB (-20.5 KiB, 38 -> 36 chunks) and /live eager 139.1 -> 132.0 KiB (-7.1 KiB, 13 -> 12 chunks). The vocabularies are re-homed, not copied — one tuple per closed set, so `@musterd/protocol` and `/wire` cannot disagree — and `guards.drift`-style coverage in packages/protocol/src/guards.test.ts runs readMemberSummary and MemberSummarySchema over one 44-row corpus asserting identical accept/reject/normalize, so the per-row ADR 148 tolerance the roster's `unreadable` count reports stays exactly as strict as the schema. The response readers (lane board/result, audit, report, seed list) deliberately check the response envelope and fill the older-daemon defaults rather than re-deriving the daemon's field validation: in the browser that check had no consumer, and a strict parse of a NEWER daemon's response is the ADR 148 failure fetchRoster was rewritten to stop.
